t:8c658f6d6f48: Jobs, 25, tells Apple's story from the garage to the Apple II. He calls the computer a "bicycle for the mind", talks about VisiCalc and ease of use, and sketches where personal computing is heading.
t:e8484f0e1cf7: Raw ABC 20/20 footage shot at Apple's offices on 18 Feb 1981, with reporter Bob Brown. Jobs, 25, explains why personal computers matter; unedited, so you see the crew between takes.
t:e16465a77172: Jobs, 28, gives his "The Future Isn't What It Used to Be" talk to designers: the history of computers, industrial design and how media evolves. Apple exists, he says, because it found the "fractional horsepower computer" five years before anyone else.
t:2a91330003ee: Apple's full 24 Jan 1984 meeting at the Flint Center. Jobs shows the "1984" ad, pulls the Mac out of a bag and it says "Hello, I'm Macintosh". It ends with a Q&A with the Mac team.
t:1fe9ec0d0469: Jobs unveils the Macintosh: the "1984" ad, demos of MacWrite and MacPaint, the Mac introducing itself, and a standing ovation.
t:922abd5e4e8c: At the Apple II Forever event in April 1984, Jobs reviews the Mac's first 100 days, with about 70,000 sold, and shows the software already written for it.
